extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: A real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring 40K video frames from video sequences across diverse environments, including crowded indoor and outdoor scenes with various lighting conditions. The dataset consists of paired top-bottom images with corresponding depth maps, captured from a robot navigating in dynamic human environments.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbiere, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi
extraction.citeAs: Zayene et al., HELVIPAD: A Real-World Dataset for Omnidirectional Stereo Depth Estimation, arXiv:2411.18335v2, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected using a custom-built rig equipped with two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and a synchronized Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor. The rig was mounted on a remotely controlled robot chassis and navigated through dynamic indoor and outdoor scenes on a university campus. Synchronization was achieved using a hardware-triggered flash.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: LiDAR point clouds are sparse, covering only a fraction of total pixels. Depth completion was used to address this sparsity. Occlusions were not explicitly handled but minimized by the small LiDAR-camera baseline.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of 29 video sequences captured between December 2023 and February 2024. It includes equirectangular images from two 360° cameras (Ricoh Theta V) and LiDAR point clouds (Ouster OS1-64).
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: A fully automated depth completion pipeline was developed. It uses temporally aggregated point clouds (4 preceding and 4 succeeding frames) and interpolates depth on spherical grid points using k-nearest neighbors. Points with high uncertainty or lacking nearby measurements are filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: LiDAR point clouds were projected onto equirectangular images using optimized rotation and translation transformations. Depth values were converted to disparity. Images were cropped to remove unnecessary regions (sky, ground) and downsized from 3840x1920 to 1920x512 pixels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data synchronization was performed using a hardware flash trigger. LiDAR frames were downsampled to match the camera frame rate (one out of every three camera frames retained). Images were cropped and downsized. Depth labels were augmented using depth completion to increase label density from ~12% to ~61%.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Ground truth depth and disparity labels were generated by projecting 3D LiDAR point clouds onto the equirectangular camera images. The projection was calibrated using a chessboard pattern. Disparity was calculated from depth using the camera baseline and polar angles.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Alignment accuracy was assessed by calculating pixel error between projected LiDAR points and image positions, resulting in an average error of 1.7 pixels. Depth completion quality was validated by splitting LiDAR point clouds into training and test sets and computing depth estimation metrics.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor, Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras, NVIDIA Jetson Xavier, ROS (Robot Operating System)
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains images of pedestrians in public spaces (indoor corridors, outdoor squares, footpaths).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance omnidirectional stereo depth estimation for mobile robots in dynamic human environments, supporting applications like autonomous driving, healthcare, and agriculture. It addresses the scarcity of real-world datasets for omnidirectional imaging.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is collected on a university campus, which may limit generalization to other types of environments. The scenes include specific lighting conditions (day, night) and weather (cloudy, sunny), but may not represent all global variations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: LiDAR data is sparse. The dataset is limited to a university campus environment. Fast-moving objects like cars may introduce errors in temporal aggregation. The depth completion pipeline does not provide labels at object boundaries. Indoor-trained models show limitations in generalizing to outdoor scenes, particularly at night.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Benchmarking of stereo depth estimation models, specifically for omnidirectional images. It is intended for developing models capable of navigating in human environments.
